_README: Venues to add to a directory without waiting for the quarterly refresh.
The mirror of closed-venues.json. That file removes places the research
would wrongly list; this one adds places it cannot find — usually because
they have not opened, so nothing is written about them in the present tense
and a search returns a plan rather than a restaurant.
Costs nothing: a data file merged deterministically on every weekly run. No
extra API call, no directory regeneration. An addition appears the next
Friday rather than waiting up to a quarter.
Fields: 'section' is one of restaurants, hotels, shops, artEntertainment,
gymsRecreation. Everything else matches the normal directory schema.
'openingFrom' (ISO date, optional): before that date the venue lists as
Coming Soon, on or after it as New. So an opening can be queued weeks ahead
and flips itself on the day, with no second edit and no window in which
something is described as open before it is.
With no 'openingFrom', an explicit notable of 'Coming Soon' stays Coming
Soon until edited — the right state when an opening is expected but the date
An entry is skipped automatically once the quarterly refresh finds the venue
on its own, and the run says so, which is the signal to delete it here.

north-waterfront.name: Julius' Castle
north-waterfront.description: The 1924 Telegraph Hill landmark below Coit Tower, reopening after nearly two decades closed following a restoration of its fire-damaged turret and original wood panelling.
north-waterfront._note: Not open as of 30 August 2026. Owner Paul Scott told reporters in July that it would reopen in September serving dinner; Brian expects October or November. No openingFrom is set precisely because the date is unknown — it stays Coming Soon until someone adds a date or changes notable to New. Delete this entry once the quarterly refresh lists it on its own.
